description: SereneDB test-config for the vendored duckdb_spatial test suite. GEOS, PROJ and GDAL are all built; GDAL uses GDAL_BUILD_OPTIONAL_DRIVERS=OFF with an explicit driver allowlist, so tests needing a driver outside that list are expected to fail -- see tests/duckdb/README.md.

skip_tests.reason: Geometry zonemap pruning is disabled. spatial's GeometryPredicatePruneCallback reads per-child statistics through FunctionStatisticsPruneInput, using input.function.GetChildren() and input.ChildStats(idx); SereneDB's DuckDB predates that and its FunctionStatisticsPruneInput carries only bind_data and a single stats reference. TryGetGeometryPredicateOperands in src/spatial/util/geometry_predicate_stats.hpp is therefore stubbed to return false, which degrades the callback to NO_PRUNING_POSSIBLE -- correct results, no zonemap elimination. This file asserts that a predicate against a constant outside the column's extent collapses the plan to EMPTY_RESULT; it gets a real scan instead. Restoring it means either forward-porting the richer prune input into the vendored DuckDB or waiting for a DuckDB bump that carries it.

Needs a GDAL driver outside our allowlist. GDAL is built with GDAL_BUILD_OPTIONAL_DRIVERS=OFF and OGR_BUILD_OPTIONAL_DRIVERS=OFF plus an explicit set (GeoJSON, GeoJSONSeq, ESRIJSON, TopoJSON, CSV, FlatGeobuf, OGR_VRT), which keeps the GDAL build tractable -- 1853 source files -- and avoids vendoring further libraries. These files need drivers we deliberately excluded: Shapefile (also disabled because GDAL's internal shapelib target collides with duckdb_spatial's own vendored shapelib, which already backs ST_ReadSHP), OpenFileGDB, XLSX, and the GDAL COPY/write path. st_write_basic and gdal_axis_order each have one passing assertion before the driver-dependent one.

The persistent RTREE index is not built (SPATIAL_USE_RTREE=OFF). SereneDB indexes geometry through `USING inverted` (iresearch/S2), so spatial's index type, its CREATE INDEX plan, its rtree_index_* pragmas and its scan-pushdown optimizer pass are compiled out rather than merely rejected by the CREATE INDEX access-method whitelist. Every file in test/sql/index/ exercises that index, so the whole directory is skipped. The in-memory FlatRTree that accelerates spatial joins is a separate per-query structure, is still built, and its tests (test/sql/join/) still run.

Needs a GDAL driver that requires GDAL_USE_SQLITE3, which is off. sqlite3 is vendored only for PROJ's embedded proj.db, and GeoPackage's spatial index is a SQLite R*Tree virtual table we do not compile in, so the sqlite, gpkg and mvt drivers are all disabled. st_read_gpkg_fid reads a GeoPackage. The two ST_AsMVT files still exercise the writer -- spatial's MVT module is protozero-based and unaffected -- but verify it by reading the tile back through GDAL's MVT driver; st_asmvtgeom and st_tileenvelope do not read back and still run.
